editorNote: Today's edition: a $83 IPO pricing, a new frontier model with a price tag, a seven-bug Ruby patch day, a PHP release, a memory-price forecast with caveats, and a government quietly running chat on open protocols.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share; trading on Nasdaq as ANT begins today
stories.summary: Anthropic priced 980 million Class A shares at $83.00 — 956.4 million sold by the company and 23.6 million by selling stockholders — with a 30-day option for underwriters to buy up to 147 million more. Closing is expected Nov. 20.
stories.whyItMatters: The pricing follows the Nov. 12 plan for trading today and ends the build-up that earlier coverage had tracked since the filing.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3/$15 per million tokens with a 1M-token context window
stories.summary: Google positions Neon between Gemini 4 Carbon (hardest long-horizon work) and Hydrogen (fast everyday tasks). It is rolling out in the Gemini API paid tier, Antigravity and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers, and Google cites an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 61 (#3) and a #1 Coding Agent Index score of 58.6.
stories.whyItMatters: Google's own benchmark claims and price list are now public for a model aimed at high-frequency engineering and knowledge work; independent results are what to wait for.

stories.headline: Ruby patches seven memory-safety flaws in Regexp and case conversion; PoCs exist, 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 fix them
stories.summary: The Nov. 18 advisory lists seven bugs, several with possible remote code execution, affecting Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9; Ruby 3.2 and older are end-of-life and unpatched. Veria Labs says one of them, a one-byte heap overflow when upcasing legacy-encoded strings, is reachable unauthenticated in default Rails and classic Sinatra and that a proof of concept will follow about a week after the advisory.
stories.whyItMatters: Anything running an affected Ruby, including bundled copies such as GitLab and GitHub Enterprise Server per Veria, needs the patched interpreter before the public exploit lands.

stories.headline: PHP 8.6 ships with partial function application, a Duration class and a polling API
stories.summary: The release adds `?` placeholders for partial function application, `\Time\Duration`, `clamp()`, an `Io\Poll` API without stream_select's 1024-connection limit, and post-quantum key encapsulation in Sodium. Session cookies become HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax by default, and `return` inside `finally` is deprecated.
stories.whyItMatters: The secure-session defaults and deprecations can change behaviour on upgrade, so they belong in the migration checklist alongside the new features.

stories.headline: A storage blog expects SSD prices to start falling in the second half of 2027, with caveats
stories.summary: DriveVault cites ComputerBase's tracker putting SSDs about 129% above September 2025 and TrendForce's view that NAND supply returns to balance in the second half of 2027, helped by weaker PC demand and YMTC's growth. It also notes memory contract prices should stay elevated in 2027 and that faster agentic AI adoption could absorb the extra supply.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a forecast built on a trade-research view, not a price change, and the post itself says 'balance' means prices stop rising rather than returning to 2024 levels.

sourceLinks.title: SSD prices will start going down the second half of next year (DriveVault)

stories.headline: The European Commission runs Matrix chat for more than 40,000 staff, alongside Teams
stories.summary: Element says the Commission moved from a summer-2025 start through a December 2025 proof of concept to a three-month laptop rollout that ended in September 2026, on Element Server Suite Pro hosted by sovereign cloud providers with EU Login sign-in. Mobile rollout and federation are still being explored.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a vendor account of a large public-sector deployment on an open protocol, and it says Matrix complements rather than replaces Teams, Signal and WhatsApp.

sourceLinks.title: How the European Commission rolled out Matrix to more than 40,000 staff (Element)
